Kraus modular elimination sieve testing Frobenius trace differences for p in [5501, 6500].

trace_collision_density.instructions: For newforms 72a1 and 144a1 and prime exponent p >= 5501, what is the expected density of auxiliary primes q = 2kp + 1 that successfully avoid trace collisions a_q(E) = a_q(f)?

criteria.high_success_rate: High success rate (>95%): almost every prime p is eliminated with small multiplier k <= 20.
criteria.moderate_success_rate: Moderate success rate: requires larger multipliers k up to 50 due to occasional trace collisions.
criteria.persistent_obstruction: Persistent obstruction: infinite family of trace collisions precluding modular elimination.

kraus_rigor_soundness.instructions: Does the existence of an auxiliary prime q = 2kp + 1 with prod_{f in S_2(N)} (a_q(E_{A,B}) - a_q(f)) != 0 mod p unconditionally prove that no non-trivial solution to A^3 + B^3 = C^p can have residual representation isomorphic to rho_{f, p}?

criteria.true: Yes, Kraus local Frobenius trace difference strictly refutes the mod-p Galois isomorphism.
criteria.false: No, residual representation may still match even if Frobenius traces differ at q.
